News.title: Fresh foreign aid farce as £13m of taxpayers’ cash helps Mozambique sell gas while Brit families face soaring bills
News.content:
MORE than £13million in UK taxpayer cash is helping Mozambique profit from flogging ­natural gas.

It comes despite new drilling being banned in the North Sea, stopping Britain from getting similar returns.



The Foreign Office has funnelled money to the East African state to help it better collect revenues and manage finances.

The project was set up in 2018 to ensure Mozambique state can “reap the imminent benefits of gas revenues”.



The UK gets no return on its investment.

The £13.2million Tax and Economic Governance Programme runs until at least the end of 2026.



It could instead fund annual energy bills of nearly 9,000 struggling British families or restore £300 Winter Fuel Payments for 44,000 pensioners.

Mozambique is soon set to rake in around £4.6billion a year from selling gas and taxes on firms operating in its territory.

Critics slammed the double standard and called for Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband to scrap the deal.

Reform’s Robert Jenrick said: “This is nuts. Reform will slash foreign aid and get drilling again in the North Sea.”



The Foreign Office said: “The Tax and Economic Governance programme helps prevent money-laundering and strengthens Mozambique’s ability to identify and remove funding that could be directed to terrorist groups, protecting the UK both at home and abroad.”

News.title: Man, 75, dead & woman rushed to hospital after fire rips through building as at least 3 others left needing treatment
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FIRE TRAGEDY Man, 75, dead & woman rushed to hospital after fire rips through building as at least 3 others left needing treatment

A 75-YEAR-OLD man has died with a woman raced to hospital after a horror fire tore through a building.

At least three other people were treated for smoke inhalation at the scene after the blaze broke out at a property on Ridgway Road in Shelton, Stoke on Trent.

Emergency services, including an air ambulance, scrambled to the property where they found the elderly man dead.

The building was evacuated and fire crews eventually managed to extinguish the flames.





The force are working with Staffordshire Fire and Rescue Service to establish what started the fire.

Police added that the man’s next of kin have been informed and his family are being supported by specialist officers.

They are appealing for any witnesses to come forward.

A spokesperson for Staffordshire Police said: “A man has sadly died and four others suffered smoke inhalation following a fire in a property in Shelton.

“We were alerted to a fire by colleagues at Staffordshire Fire and Rescue Service in a property on Ridgway Road at around 12:50pm today.

“Fire crews extinguished the fire quickly and the building was evacuated.

“Sadly, a man aged 75 was found deceased and four others were treated for smoke inhalation, with one woman in her 60s being taken to hospital.

“The next of kin have been informed and are being supported by specially-trained officers.



“A scene has been set up whilst we work with fire investigators to determine how the fire started.

“Anyone with information about the fire should call 101 quoting incident 432 of 8 August.”

News.title: Strait of Hormuz could soon reopen as deal between Iran and Oman looms, US official claims
News.content:
THE Strait of Hormuz could soon reopen as a deal between Iran and Oman looms, a US official has claimed.

They said progress was made in talks between the nations, which sit on either side of the Strait.



A deal between Iran and Oman over control of the strategic ­waterway is seen as crucial to a wider peace agreement in the US’s five-month war with Iran.

The official, who did not want to be named, said: “There is progress between Oman and Iran, and we expect a deal soon.



“Once it is announced to restore commercial shipping without impediments, the United States will lift the blockade of Iranian ports.”

Before President Donald Trump and Israel launched the war on Iran, about one in five barrels of oil consumed worldwide went through the Strait.



But Iran has fired on ships that try to cross without permission.

Meanwhile, Lebanon and Israel have agreed on a shortlist of countries to ­verify the disarmament of terror group Hezbollah.

It is part of a US- brokered deal to end the war in Lebanon.

News.title: It’ll be a disaster if early release scheme isn’t halted – child abusers, wife beaters & cop killers must stay locked up
News.content:
ANDY Burnham’s first act as prime minister has been to approve the early release of paedophiles, grooming gang members and killers – like the killers of Andrew Harper – from prison.

Labour have finally U-turned on releasing rapists, but only after weeks of pressure from Conservatives, campaigners and victims.



It is a relief that they have – but you need only look to the despair of PC Harper’s widow, Lissie, to see this is only a very partial victory.

Labour’s Justice Secretary, Alex Norris, actually apologised to her on the very day the new exclusion for rapists was announced, knowing that her husband’s killers would still go free.



On the same day, the Prime Minister had the gall to say he felt the victims’ pain.

Burnham and Labour have completely misread the public mood.



Most of us think killers, rapists and paedophiles already serve sentences that are too short.

Now, thousands will be released after serving half or as little as one third of their sentence.

We are told the public will be safe because of advanced tagging and strict licences, but we know that recalls to prison are up 28% and offenders are breaking their licences consequence-free – last year one prisoner released early went 50 days without a tag before anyone noticed.

Labour’s ex Prisons Minister, Lord Timpson, shockingly said it was impossible to know exactly which criminals would be released, where, or when.



Calculations by the Conservatives revealed that 9,300 domestic abusers stand to be let out early, and over 350 criminals guilty of manslaughter.

We are told that only “less serious” child abusers will be released early – what kind of child abuse is “less serious”?

Victims’ rights campaigners are rightly outraged.

We are told the Government has no choice.

But they said that before – and then they conjured up a thousand spaces to stop rapists being released.



If they were not telling the truth then, why should we believe them now?

Analysis by my party shows there are 4,000 usable prison spaces the Government could use.

It is wrong that criminals who have killed police officers should be set free. There are only two of these eligible for early release in the prison estate. Two.

Are Labour really saying – having just found 1,000 slots – they can’t find room for those who have taken the lives of police?

And Labour are not even building the spaces they say they are. When you factor in prison cells that are being mothballed or labelled unfit for purpose, the number of available places in prison actually fell by 400 last year. They say they are building prisons faster than ever before – it’s just not true.



Burnham has so far failed to tell us how he is going to stop rapists being released. Parliament isn’t currently sitting, and they need to change the law to stop this before it starts. We have called on Labour to pass an emergency law the day Parliament comes back.

But when we have asked them to spell out the plan, we have had silence. They must push back the start of the release scheme and use the time to change the law as a matter of urgency to keep dangerous criminals behind bars.

A disaster is unfolding as dangerous criminals are set to be let back onto our streets. But despite asking repeatedly, Labour won’t tell us the plan.

How long before a released killer strikes again, and we are all grieving over yet another tragedy?

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It would cost Labour nothing to act quickly to ensure criminals who have killed our brave police officers are kept behind bars. They risk their lives every day for our safety – it’s the least they can do to show gratitude and care for them, and for their families.



Burnham must keep child abusers, wife beaters, grooming gang members and cop killers locked up – where they belong.

News.title: ‘Coronation Street’ rapist’s cause of death confirmed after vile predator died aged 69 while locked away in prison
News.content:
SERIAL PREDATOR ‘Coronation Street’ rapist’s cause of death confirmed after vile predator died aged 69 while locked away in prison

THE cause of death for the “Coronation Street” rapist has been confirmed after the vile predator died in prison.

Andrew Davies was aged 69 when he died earlier this year while serving out 13 life sentences for a spree of horrific crimes throughout the 1980s in Greater Manchester and beyond.



Davies, who died on February 28, died from natural causes after contracting brain cancer, a report from the Prisons and Probation Ombudsman has disclosed.

He largely carried out his attacks in the Manchester area and became known as the Coronation Street rapist because his victims mainly lived in terraced houses in the north of England.



The predator would often break into the homes of victims and use weapons to threaten them, and in one case caused injury, before assaulting them.

Davies, who was locked up at Category C prison, HMP Moorland, was set free after 34 years behind bars but was recalled just six weeks later after breaching his licence conditions.

Prior to his release, the Parole Board rejected an application from then Justice Minister and Deputy PM, Dominic Raab, to cancel his scheduled release.

He was recalled just six weeks later after breaching his licence conditions and his application for parole was denied in 2024.

The report reads: “In October 2017, Mr Andrew Davies was sentenced to life imprisonment for sexual offences.

“He died of brain cancer on 28 February 2026, at HMP Moorland.



“He was 69 years old. We offer our condolences to Mr Davies’ family and friends.

“The Ombudsman’s office wrote to Mr Davies’ next of kin to explain the investigation and to ask if they had any matters they wanted us to consider. They did not respond.”

The statement added: “They found no factual inaccuracies. At the inquest, held on 8 April 2026, the Coroner concluded that Mr Davies died from natural causes.”

His death has come as a relief to his victims, with one telling Manchester Evening News it was a “very difficult feeling to handle”.

In 1987, Davies had raped her in her own bed at knifepoint and she said “I still relive what he did to me”.



He also attacked a 26-year-old woman in her Sheffield home while her terrified three-year-old daughter hid behind a settee.

In 1988, he was sentenced for raping 11 women and slapped with 11 life sentences with an additional 56 years for other offences.

He was then handed an additional two life sentences in 2010 and 2017 respectively for rapes he committed in 1981 and 1982.

News.title: Teen, mum & grandma die after tourist helicopter crashes & sparks huge fire as devastated family watched on from hangar
News.content:
FOUR people have been killed in a horror helicopter crash during a birthday trip for a teenage girl.

Three members of the same Colombian family and the pilot died when the Robinson R44 helicopter crashed in the Vista Chinesa region, south of Rio de Janeiro.



Harrowing footage shows firefighters battling to reach the still-burning wreckage as flames engulfed the aircraft.

All four people on board were killed in the resulting blaze.



Firefighters were called to the scene shortly after 11am, with 40 emergency personnel and 11 vehicles sent to the crash site.

But rescuers faced a treacherous operation, with the helicopter coming down in a steep, wooded area surrounded by cliffs.



The victims have been named as grandmother Rocio Cubillos, 59, mother Wendy Manrique, 37, and daughter Sofia, 17.

The pilot, Alessandro Rocha, was also killed.



Rocha was reportedly an experienced pilot with more than 20 years in the industry.

He is survived by his partner and three children – two boys and a girl.

The three Colombian tourists were reportedly on their first trip to Brazil.

They arrived on Monday and were due to remain in the country until Tuesday.

According to relatives, the family booked the helicopter tour after researching operators on social media.



Rocio’s son, Vitor Manrique, his wife Daniela Castañeda and their 15-year-old daughter were waiting for the family to return at the hangar.

The family had booked the helicopter ride to celebrate the teenager’s birthday.

They became alarmed after hearing an employee say there had been a “forced landing”.

The relatives said they repeatedly asked staff what had happened, but were given no information.

They eventually learned of their relatives’ fate through news websites while they were still waiting at the hangar.



Lieutenant Colonel Fábio Contreiras said rescuers faced major difficulties reaching the crash site.

“The biggest challenge for the teams right now is access, both to enter and exit the site,” he said.

“The aircraft crashed in a very steep, wooded area with precipitous cliffs, where it is only possible to work using rope techniques and safety equipment.”

He added that a fire had broken out following the crash after the aircraft’s fuel ignited.

“When we arrived, in addition to the helicopter, there was also a fire caused by the explosion of the aircraft’s fuel. That fire has now been completely extinguished,” he said.



“Now, our challenge is to find faster access routes to facilitate the work of the Civil Police and Cenipa forensics teams, as well as the future removal of the bodies.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The exact cause of the crash remains unknown.

The Brazilian Air Force said an investigation is underway to establish what caused the helicopter to come down.

News.title: Women will be killed as a result of Government’s ‘unsafe’ early release scheme, probation bosses warns
News.content:
PROBATION bosses are warning women will be killed because of the ­Government’s “unsafe” early release scheme, The Sun on Sunday can reveal.

The union Napo, which ­represents probation and court staff, has also declared no ­confidence in the Prison and Probation Service.



Bosses are now balloting on strike action after slamming PM Andy Burnham and Justice Secretary Alex Norris in a message to members.

Mr Burnham has been forced to roll back parts of the “unfit” release programme after a public backlash.



Serious sex offenders including rapists will now be excluded from the plan.

But there will be no change to manslaughter cases — meaning two of the killers of PC Andrew Harper’s killers are due out.



Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole will be eligible to leave prison after serving half their sentences.

A petition against the thugs’ early release has passed 810,000 signatures.

In total, from next month the number of offenders monitored by tags, which are overseen by ­probation workers, will hit 40,000 — up from 28,000 earlier this year.

Ministers are now said to be looking at further U-turns in the first major scandal of Mr Burnham’s premiership.



Napo says the reversals do not go far enough, warning in a major intervention that ministers have failed to “address the real issues of public and safe releases”.

The union wrote to members: “The Prime Minister and the Justice Secretary have failed to ­acknowledge the probation workloads crisis that has afflicted the service for over two years.”

A senior union source said “plans to release thousands of domestic abuse perpetrators and stalkers early” mean “more people, largely women, will be killed or harmed”.

Ian Lawrence, Napo’s General Secretary, told The Sun on Sunday: “Everyone is talking about prisons, and yes it is bad, but the crisis in probation is far worse. But yet again, our members are being overlooked while all the attention is on prison.”

Shadow safeguarding minister Alicia Kearns told The Sun on Sunday: “Probation officers are the last line of defence between dangerous men and the women they target. When they warn Labour’s early release scheme will get women murdered, every minister should be shamed into acting to protect us. Scrap this scheme now.”



The Ministry of Justice said “Our record £700million investment in probation and community punishment is ensuring staff have the resources and powers to manage offenders safely in the community.”

News.title: Andy Burnham suggested FORCING  private landlords to sell rental homes just months before becoming PM
News.content:
ANDY Burnham suggested private landlords should be forced to sell their rental homes just months before becoming PM.

He called for more “public control” of housing so that properties could be made energy-efficient “quickly” to meet green targets.



Speaking at an eco-summit in March when he was Mayor of Greater Manchester, Mr Burnham said: “We can, if necessary, take homes out of the private rented sector and put them into the public housing stock so that we can give people homes that are cheaper to rent and cheaper to run.”

Shadow energy minister Andrew Bowie said: “Under the guise of Net Zero, Andy Burnham wants to send officers of the state to your door and take your home.



“We should just make electricity cheap and let people choose what works for them, rather than threatening repossession.”

Sources said Mr Burnham was specifically talking about Manchester and that his ideas at the time are not government policy.



Under Mr Burnham, Greater Manchester set a target of carbon neutrality by 2038 which includes steps to improve homes.

He also previously called for private rental properties that do not meet legal requirements in the Decent Homes Standard to be bought by councils through compulsory purchase orders.

News.title: Andy Burnham to embark on cost of living tour through the UK
News.content:
The prime minister is set to announce "a series of measures to make life easier" for those struggling with the cost of living in the coming days, Downing Street says.

No 10 says Andy Burnham's plans are to "give people some room to breathe". He will also focus on ways of "improving high streets" as he embarks on a tour of the UK.

But the government is facing continued pressure over its early release scheme for prisoners in England and Wales â with criticism of the fact that two of PC Andrew Harper's killers will be eligible from next year.

Burnham is also likely to face pressure for more action on the cost of living â although significant interventions are unlikely before October's Budget.

Even then, Chancellor John Healey has made it clear he will oversee "strong fiscal discipline" â which will limit how much the government has to spend.

The prime minister has been on holiday this week, but Downing Street said he would be in "listening mode" in the coming days as he tours the UK's nations and regions and works on a "10-year plan to bring back hope".

A spokesman for the prime minister said: "He thinks Westminster has got used to telling people that everyday hassles â like hidden pricing and consumers being ripped off â must be accepted as part of life.

"He doesn't think that's right. That's why he's going to start rolling out a series of pro-consumer cost of living measures to give people some room to breathe."

The spokesman added: "He's also going to be kicking off his summer tour around the country, getting out of Westminster and meeting people where they are.

"The prime minister is going to be in listening mode to help inform his 10-year plan to bring back hope and make Britain better off."

There are, though, likely to be continued questions about the forthcoming early release scheme, due to start in October.

One of Burnham's first acts in Downing Street was to order a review which limited the range of people who would be eligible.

But those convicted of manslaughter will still qualify for the scheme â including two of the killers of PC Andrew Harper.

The prime minister has faced calls from PC Harper's family, former senior police officers and opposition politicians for them to be denied early release.

But he has said he cannot go any further without risking prison capacity. Downing Street said on Saturday night that position remained unchanged, despite reports the prime minister could revisit the case.

The Conservatives said the government's "tax hikes and red tape are hammering our high streets".

Shadow chancellor Mel Stride said: "This is breathtaking hypocrisy from Burnhamâ¦ they are forcing businesses to close, destroying jobs and driving up prices for the public.

"Meanwhile, Labour are plotting to release dangerous criminals onto our streets, leaving people feeling unsafe in their communities."

Liberal Democrat Treasury spokeswoman Daisy Cooper said struggling high street businesses "need more than a new PM embarking on a vanity tour this summer".

She said the PM should adopt the Lib Dem plan for high streets: "That means reversing the damaging jobs tax, delivering an emergency VAT cut for hospitality, replacing broken business rates and cracking down on the ghost landlords leaving our shop fronts vacant."

Reform UK's economic spokesman Robert Jenrick said: "If Andy Burnham wants to help people with the cost of living, he should scrap the green levies and taxes on energy bills and rule out tax rises at the Budget."

News.title: Fifa criticises campaign to oust president Infantino
News.content:
Fifa has strongly criticised what it calls a "concerted and ongoing effort" to "undermine" the organisation and its president Gianni Infantino.

The statement follows a Daily Telegraph report, external which claimed Infantino's alleged lover was given a severance payment by Uefa after he had an affair while he was its general secretary.

A Fifa spokesperson told the Telegraph Infantino "strongly denies" the allegations and that they are "categorically untrue".

Fifa has now itself hit out at "unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims", adding that "speculation and insinuation should not be presented as fact".

Infantino has come under increasing pressure from Uefa and European football associations over his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

FFE would have meant a new company being created to manage commercial and ticketing rights, with 21% sold off to a private investment company.

Uefa has said it has lost confidence in Infantino, while Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) president Lise Klaveness on Friday called on the Swiss-Italian to resign.

European football's governing body says its threat to boycott Fifa events remains on the table, adding that assurances the FFE plan could not be revived have not been received.

"The Fifa president was democratically elected by Fifa's Member Associations and continues to serve with their mandate," Fifa said in its statement on Saturday.

"It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president.

"Those who do not have the support of Fifa's member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa's established democratic processes."

Opposition to Infantino is largely from within Europe.

The Mexican Football Federation broke ranks with its regional governing body Concacaf to come out in support of Infantino.

It echoed a statement from Conmebol - South America's governing body - in saying it would reject any attempt to remove Infantino without a vote involving all 211 Fifa member countries.

Infantino is also unanimously backed by the 54 nations of the Confederation of African Football (Caf).

News.title: Killed a month after his wedding - why PC Andrew Harper's death touched so many
News.content:
On the night of 15 August 2019, Lissie Harper got a knock at the door. She thought it was her husband Andrew coming home from work.

Instead, it was uniformed officers, there to tell her that the man she had married four weeks earlier had been killed while on police duty.

"Everything I had known in my life to be true was robbed away. Every ounce of beautiful peace, gone," Lissie later said of the moment she was told.

They had met as teenagers and were together for 13 years.

In her eulogy at his funeral, Lissie recalled how Andrew would pass her notes in class.

They were, she said, "true childhood sweethearts, loving one another more and more with each passing day".

They had been about to go on their honeymoon.

But, on that night nearly seven years ago, everything changed.

The case has been back in the headlines because two of PC Harper's killers â Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole â will become eligible to be released early under government plans to tackle prison overcrowding.

As the disturbing details of the case are revisited, his family, fellow officers and the public are outraged once more â at what happened, and at the perpetrators' impending release.

PC Harper's death was brutal and devastating, causing shock, anger and an outpouring of grief across the country.

Pictures of the smiling faces of his teenage killers laughing and joking as they left court only added to that anger.

PC Harper had been about to head home at the end of a long shift when he and a colleague were called to reports of a burglary.

He was "going beyond the call of duty", the prosecutor at the Old Bailey trial in 2020 said.

During the case, haunting dashcam footage from the police patrol car was played showing the moment PC Harper confronted teenagers Henry Long, Bowers and Cole down a dark country lane. He then disappeared from view.

His ankles had got caught in a strap trailing behind the car being driven by Long that had been used to tow a stolen quad bike.

PC Harper was dragged for over a mile. He died on the road. His police badge and stab vest were found scattered along the route.

The three teenagers were tried for murder. In the end, the jury convicted Bowers and Cole of manslaughter. Long had already pleaded guilty to that offence.

It meant the jury was not sure that PC Harper's killers knew they were dragging the officer behind the car.

But the Judge, Mr Justice Edis, described it as a manslaughter case which was "very close to a case of murder" in its seriousness.

News.title: Israel accused of weaponising archaeology at ancient West Bank sites
News.content:
Up in the hills above the Roman columns of the ancient site of Sebastia, in the occupied West Bank, are olive fields that have been cultivated for generations by Palestinian families.

One of the landowners, Abu Mudif, says he has received notification that his land is part of a tranche of about 450 acres that the Israeli authorities are taking possession of in order, they say, to protect and develop the site for a major new national park.

Typically, Palestinian landowners receive little or no payment for such land expropriation. And even when it is offered, most refuse it as they see accepting it as giving recognition and legitimacy to the loss of what they see as their patrimony.

It's a vital income for Abu Mudif to lose of course, but it goes deeper than that for him.

News.title: Australia is the planet's extinction hotspot, but one animal offers a glimmer of hope
News.content:
"Eyes peeled," comes the order from the front passenger seat.

Obediently, we scan the ends and tops of logs, looking between low scrub and patches of vivid wildflowers for a flash of stripes or a dart of movement.

Eluding us is the numbat, a rare Australian marsupial which could be the love-child of a chipmunk and an anteater.

Numbats were once populous across the bottom half of the continent, but Dryandra Woodland â in the south-western corner of Australia â is one of the few places they remain.

As we slowly roll along bush tracks, researchers explain how this annual trip helps plot the species' survival.

Classified as endangered until this month, numbats have been bouncing back. This team's efforts have seen them scratched off the international red list of threatened species - a rare glimmer of hope in a country facing an extinction emergency.

This part of Australia is the front line of that crisis: a last stand for many species driven to the brink by feral pests, disease, urban development, habitat destruction and climate change.

Winging over our car at one point is the endangered Carnaby's cockatoo. On an island just off the coast is one of the last surviving pockets of the world's rarest marsupial, the Gilbert's potoroo. Diving in the sapphire waters around it is the increasingly scarce Australian sea lion.

News.title: More areas of UK likely to move into drought as fifth heatwave builds
News.content:
Sunday will be a warmer day across many areas with temperatures widely getting up to the mid to high twenties Celsius. South-east England will be even hotter where temperatures will rise to over 30C and possibly as high as 33C.

This will break the record for the highest number of days on which the temperature has exceeded 30C somewhere in the UK. The previous record was 34 days in 1995.

After a cooler day on Monday, temperatures will then rise widely across the UK from Tuesday.

In Scotland and Northern Ireland, temperatures will typically reach the low to mid twenties.

In England and Wales, temperatures will rise into the mid to high twenties Celsius and widely across east Wales, central, eastern and southern England in excess of 30C.

The heat is set to peak on Thursday, with readings of 35C possible in south-east England.

If this happens, it will be the fourth consecutive month of 35C or more being recorded.

The threshold for declaring an official heatwave is likely to be reached widely across England and Wales, making it the fifth heatwave of the year for many.

Yellow heat health alerts are in effect for most of England until 21:00 BST on Tuesday, warning of impacts for health and social care services and an increased risk to life for vulnerable people.

These are likely to be updated in the coming days as heatwave conditions develop.

News.title: Kellie Bright to leave EastEnders after 13 years
News.content:
EastEnders star Kellie Bright is to leave the soap after playing one of its key characters, Linda Carter, for 13 years.

She arrived in Albert Square with on-screen husband Mick, portrayed by Danny Dyer, when they became the new owners of the Queen Vic pub.

Carter's matriarch character has been central to major storylines including plots about murder, sexual assault and alcoholism.

Bright said she made the "tough decision" to leave more than a year ago but "happily" agreed to stay on to be part of an "exciting storyline".

The BBC has promised "unmissable drama" before her on-screen exit, which is said to be a "while away" yet.

Executive producer Ben Wadey described the actor as being "the beating heart of EastEnders" and said she had become "a classic EastEnders icon".

Viewers have seen the much-loved character at the heart of many emotional storylines including in 2014 when she was raped by her brother-in-law Dean Wicks.

More than 7m people watched the episode which prompted dozens of complaints. The sexual assualt led to long-running story arc about family conflict and trauma.

News.title: Zendaya saw me on the red carpet and her jaw dropped - I'm still in shock
News.content:
"I can't zip this! Mummm?"

This was 29-year-old Zainab Jiwa, calling out for help squeezing into a corset while filming a "get-ready-with-me" TikTok video. It's a scene many 20-somethings still living at home will relate to.

The difference is, Zainab was on her way to the recent London premiere of The Odyssey, one of the summer's biggest blockbusters.

She was invited there as a guest and says she caught the eye of Hollywood megastar Zendaya, thanks to her custom look: a striking gold gown complete with a hood.

"She just walked past, and she saw me there. Her jaw just dropped, so did mine," Zainab tells me.

"It was just a stare-off for a minute, and she was like, 'Oh my god, amazing, amazing,' and then she just walked off."

"Iâm still in shock,â she adds. âThe thought of her noticing my outfit blew my mind."

The interaction went viral, external with 19m TikTok views. Her phone blew up.

While Zendaya has been ruling the red carpets with high-fashion "method dressing" â where stars match outfits to a film's themes â Zainab is perhaps proving that independent creators like her can give Hollywood a run for its money.

Zainab, who is Muslim and wears a hijab, is also often one of the only people covering her hair at premieres, but she says finding ways to incorporate modest wear is part of the fun.

"Even though you're covered, you can still find a way to be on theme.â

News.title: Banksy works cost public almost £150,000
News.content:
Three artworks by street artist Banksy have cost taxpayers almost Â£150,000 in cleaning operations and security so far, with the bill expected to rise.

The largest single cost relates to a mural painted on the Royal Courts of Justice in September 2025, where removal efforts and security have so far cost more than Â£85,000.

The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) says it has spent Â£50,000 trying to remove paint from the wall of the Grade II-listed building in Carey Street. A further Â£35,300 was spent on overtime and security costs.

The spending was disclosed to the BBC through Freedom of Information requests and is likely to reignite debate over whether Banksy's work is vandalism or valuable public art.

News.title: Simon Levy victims urged to come forward as police accused of 'litany of failures'
News.content:
Police have urged more victims of Simon Levy to come forward, as London's victims' commissioner said a "litany of failures" had allowed him to kill two women and rape a third.

Andrea Simon called for a review on the "failure to monitor him appropriately" when the 40-year-old was known to police as a sexual predator.

British Transport Police said women who recognised Levy as their attacker should report it, while the Met Police said it had investigated whether he had more victims, including further murders.

Meanwhile, the Independent Office of Police Conduct (IOPC) said a police constable is under investigation for gross misconduct, and a detective sergeant is facing a misconduct investigation.

On Friday, Levy was found guilty of murdering two women and raping a third in London while he was being monitored by the Met Police for being a convicted sex offender. He had previously committed a string of sex attacks.

The BBC reported how a series of grave failings by police, prosecutors and the courts left Levy free to murder, rape and sexually assault women.

Levy is due to be sentenced on Wednesday.

News.title: Widdecombe police reopen investigation into incident at Farage's home, BBC understands
News.content:
Counter-terrorism police investigating the killing of Ann Widdecombe have reopened an inquiry into an incident at Nigel Farage's south London home, the BBC understands.

It is understood to relate to what the Reform UK leader described as a "lit incendiary device" being pushed through his letterbox in April 2025.

Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) London said it was looking into an "attempted burglary" at a property as part of the Widdecombe murder investigation, but did not confirm the home was linked to Farage or why it might be connected to the killing of the former MP.

CTP London has also referred itself to the police watchdog over how the initial investigation into the Farage incident was handled.

Police said at the time that "damage was caused to a door but nothing was stolen".

Both CTP London and the Metropolitan Police were involved in enquiries. No arrests were made and the investigation was closed.

But on Friday, CTP London said a new line of inquiry had been identified that was not "pursued by them at the time".

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it had "decided to independently investigate the conduct of a Counter Terrorism Policing London staff member following a referral received earlier [on Friday]".

A statement continued: "The conduct relates to an allegation the individual failed to identify and pursue a line of enquiry relating to an attempted burglary reported in April 2025."

CTP London said it would "full engage" with the watchdog's investigation, adding: "The victims and families in both investigations have been updated today, and we continue to support them."

Ann Widdecombe, the 78-year-old former Conservative minister and Reform UK spokeswoman, was found dead at her home in Devon last month with serious injuries.

Joshua Kerry, from Rotherham in South Yorkshire, was later charged with her murder.

Kerry was initially arrested on suspicion of murder on 11 July, before being additionally arrested on 13 July on suspicion of the commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism.

Widdecombe had served as Tory MP for Maidstone in Kent for 23 years and was appointed to ministerial roles in Sir John Major's government in the 1990s.

News.title: Woman attacked by bed bugs during Travelodge stay
News.content:
Thirteen days after Hannah Stephenson stayed a night in a Travelodge hotel, she is still itching with red lumps over her body - a nightmare she would not wish on her "worst enemy".

The 31-year-old from Bassingbourn had been out with friends in Cambridge and decided to book a one-night stay at the hotel on Newmarket Road on 26 July to save money instead of getting a taxi home.

The next morning, she woke up to a "horrible realisation", feeling itchy with red lumps over her body and blood spots smeared on the bedding â the tell-tale signs of bed bugs, she said.

A Travelodge spokesperson said: "We are deeply sorry for Ms Stephenson's experience and how distressing an incident like this can be."

Stephenson said a lovely evening with friends had turned into a horrible morning.

"It was just a lovely wholesome time of Cambridge sightseeing and pubs, and now it is tarnished by these bedbug bites," she said.

"It wasn't until I saw the blood and the bugs that I realised what had happened."

News.title: Charity watchdog investigates aid charity over alleged Hamas links
News.content:
A UK-based aid charity is being investigated by counter-terror police and the charity watchdog over alleged links to Hamas.

The Charity Commission launched an inquiry into Muslim faith-based charity Al-Khair Foundation on Friday.

Counter Terror Policing London (CTP) also confirmed investigations into the charity, with two search warrants on addresses in Croydon, South London.

The foundation said it is "co-operating fully" with the inquiry and had filed a serious incident report with the watchdog before it was launched.

A spokesperson for the foundation said: "Everywhere we work we are firmly committed to ensuring that the funds entrusted to us by our generous donors are used for their intended purpose: meeting the humanitarian needs of poor and marginalised people in the communities we serve.

"Al-Khair Foundation is deeply committed to supporting those in need in Gaza. Our significant support over many years has included providing food parcels, hot meals, clean water, medical aid, shelter materials, winter assistance and orphan and family support."

The Al-Khair Foundation provides emergency relief and developmental support in "some of the world's most impoverished areas", according to its website.

Hamas is designated as a terrorist organisation by the UK and US governments.

It comes after last week Mohammad Yousef Hasna, 45, from Istanbul, Turkey, was arrested in the UK over US accusations of conspiring to funnel money and supplies to Hamas through a "sham charity".

The US Department of Justice did not name the "sham charity" in their press release.

The Al-Khair foundation maintains that Hasna is not an employee but works with one of its global partners to enable the delivery of aid around the world.

Hasna is being held following his arrest by the UK's National Crime Agency (NCA) and pending extradition proceedings before he can be taken to New York to face the US charges.

The US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York alleged Hasna used his senior role at a "purported global humanitarian organisation to coordinate directly with Hamas's senior leadership regarding the delivery of funds and supplies to Gaza, and the distribution of those funds and supplies at Hamas leadership's instructions".

Hasna is charged with conspiring to provide material support to Hamas, conspiring to finance terrorism and financing terrorism.

Each charge carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, the US Department of Justice said.

US Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg said: "The money that flows from sham charities like the one described in the complaint fuels Hamas's terrorist activities, including the atrocities the group committed on October 7".

The Charity Commission said the Al-Khair Foundation recorded an income of more than Â£74m in the financial year ending 31 July 2025. The commission added it was made aware of the allegations against Hasna and "immediately started examining the serious concerns raised".

"The commission has now escalated its engagement to a statutory inquiry," the commission added.

Al-Khair is also subject to a legal order restricting some financial transactions being made without the consent of the Charity Commission.

News.title: Strictly dancers Ola and James Jordan separate after 23 years of marriage
News.content:
Former Strictly Come Dancing stars James and Ola Jordan have confirmed they have separated after more than 20 years of marriage.

The former professional dancers were regulars on the show for several series after first featuring in 2006.

The couple in a statement said they were "taking some time apart as we work through very difficult personal challenges".

"This has been an incredibly painful and emotional journey for us both and it certainly wasn't an easy decision," they said in a joint post shared on their Instagram accounts.

The couple said James had moved out the family home some time ago and they "don't know exactly what the future holds".

"Right now, more than anything we ask for kindness, empathy and a little privacy as we work through this as a family."

The couple's manager Vickie White had prevously said in a statement: "It is with great sadness that I can confirm that James and Ola began a trial separation some time ago

"Their shared priority remains co-parenting their daughter, Ella, and they are committed to putting her wellbeing first.

"They would greatly appreciate your understanding as they navigate this difficult time."

Ola Jordan won the Open Polish Championship in 1999 when she was 17 years old and became James' dance partner shortly afterwards in March 2000.

She moved to England a month later and the pair got married in October 2003.

James appeared on Strictly from 2006 to 2013 while Ola appeared on the show until 2015.

Ola's celebrity partners included wildlife presenter Steve Backshall and Welsh sprinter Iwan Thomas, while James danced with former international gymnast and broadcaster Gabby Logan, as well as The One Show presenter Alex Jones.

News.title: Hundreds flying out of Birmingham Airport left without luggage
News.content:
She described seeing a "build up" of luggage at the airport, after problems with the luggage belt, but had been assured by staff that it would be loaded on to the plane.

But on arrival at Dalaman they were told by the pilot that no bags had been loaded.

"We have heard nothing about compensation, no communication when our luggage is expected, we've heard nothing about who is liable for it. Is it the airport? Is it TUI? Is it our travel insurance? Who are we meant to go to? We've had nothing from anybody", Chapman said.

"It's just radio silence from the airport, apart from literally telling people 'we've got an issue'".

The first day of their holiday was spent travelling to a shopping centre to buy essentials for "for the next few days" but she added "we have no idea how long this is going to last".

"There are families all over the world at the moment with nothing and no idea of what's going on," she said.

"It's really important that Birmingham Airport are held accountable, and sort this out."

News.title: Man guilty of fatal shooting of teen outside club
News.content:
A man has been found guilty of fatally shooting an 18-year-old outside a Wembley nightclub.

Tyrece Balcha was found with gunshot wounds outside the Crystal Club in Atlantic Crescent at about 05:30 GMT on 21 September 2025. He was taken to hospital, where he died four days later.

A jury at the Old Bailey found Ashley Wallace, 40, of Shenley Road, Southwark, guilty of murder and possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life.

At the same trial, two men were found not guilty of murder. A woman was cleared of possession of a firearm, possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life, and perverting the course of justice. The jury did not reach a verdict on a fourth man.

CCTV footage showed that Balcha had been involved in an altercation inside the club before being followed outside and shot.

Wallace fled the scene in a vehicle and was arrested on 25 September after police traced the car to south-east London.

A revolver carrying Wallace's DNA was found inside the vehicle, and investigators established that the bullet recovered from the murder scene had been fired from the gun.

With the Iran war draining U.S. weapons stockpiles, the Pentagon is reportedly leaning hard on defense companies to bump up production — and fast.

In a memo on Wednesday, Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg gave companies three weeks to lay out how they would “drive significantly faster, more aggressive delivery schedules and/or increased production for critical capabilities.”

“Years-long development cycles are not acceptable,” Feinberg added in the memo, which was obtained by The Washington Post. “We must dramatically accelerate our program schedules and expand our production capacity now.”

The Pentagon confirmed the existence of the August 5 memo and praised Feinberg as a “generational leader” who was “fixing our broken, antiquated, and immensely complex acquisitions system.”

“Working directly with industry leaders to accelerate production is not new,” chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell wrote in a statement to The Independent. “It has been the clear intent of the President and this Secretary from the start.”

open image in gallery The Pentagon is leaning on weapons makers to speed up production as the Iran war reportedly drains key munitions stockpiles ( US Navy )

“The fiscal year 2027 budget currently being considered on Capitol Hill could supercharge this effort today,” he added.

The demands come after weapons manufacturers were reportedly summoned to the White House in July, where they were allegedly urged to lobby Congress to pass another round of funding.

President Donald Trump has insisted the U.S. still has “massive amounts” of weapons, though tempers have reportedly flared over the issue behind the scenes.

The president reportedly confronted Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at Camp David last week over the munitions shortage, claiming he thought the problem “had been fixed” already.

open image in gallery The US has expended numerous munitions fighting off swarms of Iranian drones and missile strikes on American bases in the Middle East ( AFP/Getty )

The Trump administration has denied this account, while the president has threatened jail time for the “treasonous” leakers that fueled the reporting.

The U.S. has reportedly used nearly all of its stockpiled long-range precision missiles in the Iran conflict, according to CBS News.

The military has also burned through roughly half of its Patriot interceptors and nearly four-fifths of its Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) missile inventory compared to pre-war levels, CNN reported.

The Iran conflict has been something of a strategic mismatch. Tehran, despite possessing a much smaller military than the U.S., has pummeled American bases across the Middle East with low-cost, single-use drones, which the U.S. often has to use expensive interceptors to stop.

The U.S. military had 2,330 Patriot systems and 452 THAAD systems before the war, according to a July report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

As of July 27, the organization estimated 759 to 827 Patriot systems and 234 to 278 THAAD systems remained.

A UK university has opened a new government-funded laboratory to help train the next generation of biomedical scientists to work in the NHS and life sciences sector.

The £2.5 million facility at the University of Essex, which includes a dedicated cancer diagnostics laboratory, was funded by the Office for Students.

The investment aims to strengthen training in subjects critical to the UK’s future workforce.

The Bioscience Skills Training and Research Laboratory (BioSTAR-Lab) aims to give students hands-on experience with equipment and techniques used in modern healthcare and life sciences laboratories.

Students studying biomedical science, biotechnology, cancer biology and related degrees will use the laboratories to carry out their research projects.

The facility also includes specialist microbiology and molecular biology laboratories where students will analyse tissue samples, study infectious diseases and use molecular techniques.

open image in gallery The cancer diagnostics laboratory at the University of Essex. (University of Essex/ PA)

Professor Terry McGenity, head of the School of Life Sciences, said: “Here at Essex, we are dedicated to providing a rounded education that is inspired by our world-leading research, which equips our students with the understanding, skills and experience they need to launch their careers in nationally important sectors.

“Hands-on, lab-based research projects provide a transformative experience for our final-year undergraduates and masters students.

“They allow all our students to become part of the research process by carrying out their project alongside experts, where they apply what they’ve learned, and develop critical understanding of a particular area, as well as new technical and analytical skills.

“This new facility will place us at the forefront of training students to be skilled and versatile critical thinkers, who will be ready to work in the NHS and life-sciences sectors.”

The university said the investment comes at a time of growing demand for skilled life scientists, with more than 300,000 people already employed in the sector in the UK.

The lab’s opening comes as the University of Essex launches its first undergraduate biotechnology degree, reflecting growing demand for graduates in a sector that develops vaccines, medicines and diagnostic technologies.

open image in gallery A student examining cancer cells in the lab at the University of Essex. (University of Essex/ PA)

Professor Silke Paulmann, executive dean of the Faculty of Science and Health, said the lab “brings together education, research and real-world application, creating opportunities for students to develop the expertise that will drive future advances in diagnostics, treatments and public health”.

“It will help strengthen the talent pipeline that underpins innovation, economic growth and better health outcomes for communities across the UK,” she said.

The natural gas plant powering a sprawling Amazon data center project in Texas could become the largest climate polluter in the country, despite the company’s commitment to achieving net-zero emissions by 2040.

As part of a planned data center campus in Pecos County, the tech giant is investing in an on-site natural gas power plant, the company has confirmed.

The plant is permitted to release 33 million tons of carbon dioxide per year, according to documents obtained by The New York Times and the climate research outlet Distilled.

If the final plant matches those specifications, it would be the largest single source of climate pollution in the country, according to the Times, more than doubling the emissions from Alabama’s James H. Miller Jr. Power Plant, a coal facility which emits about 16 million tons of carbon dioxide annually. (Power plants don’t always emit the maximum they are allowed to, and the Amazon facility is still in early-stage construction.)

The company has emphasized that the power plant would not raise rates for Texas residents.

open image in gallery A future Amazon data center will be powered by a gas plant that could become the largest carbon polluter in the country, complicating the company’s climate commitments ( Getty )

“Amazon believes in paying the full costs of powering our operations,” an Amazon spokesperson said in a statement to The Independent on Saturday. “Our new planned data center campus in Pecos County does just that: it’s powered by new on-site generation that won’t raise electricity costs for Texas families and designed to transition to grid-connected service as interconnection timelines allow.”

Amazon is “exploring opportunities for solar energy and battery storage on site,” according to the company. The Pecos project is expected to create “thousands of new jobs,” Amazon said.

The site is reportedly Amazon’s first major investment in off-grid power for a data center.

This puts them in league with “hyperscalers” including Microsoft, Google and Meta, which have all invested in fossil fuel power sources this year as tech companies race to get enough data centers online to meet the ravenous demand for artificial intelligence.

The data campus is the latest complication in Amazon’s highly touted climate commitments.

The company has long faced criticism for working with fossil fuel firms, and its emissions have largely continued to rise since it unveiled its climate commitment in 2019.

open image in gallery High demand for AI has sparked both a data center boom and a power crunch, prompting tech companies to invest in new fossil fuel power sources ( Reuters )

“We recognize that the path to being a more sustainable company is not a straight line,” Amazon said in its recently released sustainability report about 2025. “Though our emissions increased in 2025, we remain steadfast in our commitment to sustainability.”

Asked about the Texas project, Amazon said it remained committed to its climate pledge and pointed to its past record of backing 40 renewable energy projects in the state.

Data centers have increasingly provoked a political backlash, with criticisms honing in on everything from the centers’ environmental emissions to their water use and impact on electricity rates.

This week, the state of Texas pause new data center projects until state electricity regulators could complete an audit of each proposed facility.

“Simply put, Texans must come first,” Republican Governor Greg Abbott wrote in a statement.

The governor’s office noted that approximately 90 percent of the new power requests on the Texas grid are for data centers — facilities that are seeking 474 gigawatts of electricity, more than five times the state’s peak electricity demand record on the grid covering most of the state.

The Trump administration has pushed to speed up data center construction, including by redeveloping federal land to host the facilities, which consume far more electricity than typical data centers and are forecast to imperil global plans to stop the climate crisis.

High demand for data centers, mixed with delays in building new grid connections and power sources, has sent tech companies in search of alternatives, ranging from building bespoke, on-site natural gas plants to investing in future nuclear reactors.

Reproductive health advocates fear newly confirmed Attorney General Todd Blanche will usher in a new wave of restrictions on abortion — even in states where it is legal.

Blanche’s confirmation “is a red alert for reproductive rights,” according to Nancy Northup, president and CEO of the Center for Reproductive Rights. “The Attorney General’s job is to fairly and faithfully enforce the law, but Blanche appears willing to contort it to score wins for political allies,” she said Saturday.

Blanche has “openly vowed to use that power to ban abortion,” Gowri Buddiga, interim managing director for the group Free & Just, said in a statement shared with The Independent Saturday.

“From promising to restrict access to medication abortion through the mail, to gutting protections for patients and providers, Blanche will roll back access to care everywhere even in states where abortion is currently protected,” Buddiga said.

Blanche, who was confirmed in the early morning hours on Saturday by a narrow 50-49 vote, alarmed abortion advocates after leaked audio captured Trump’s former criminal defense attorney vowing to make the 2022 Supreme Court decision overturning the right to an abortion “permanent in every single state.”

open image in gallery Abortion rights groups fear newly confirmed Attorney General Todd Blanche will restrict access to the procedure nationwide, after leaked audio caught Blanche telling faith leaders he was gearing up for a ‘permanent’ victory on abortion ( Reuters )

“We don’t have complete victory yet, but we will have victory, and victory will be soon, and it will be permanent,” Blanche said, according to Politico, which obtained the now-deleted clip.

“If states have said, ‘We are going to protect the unborn and we’re going to protect every life from the moment of conception,’ we’re putting practices and policies in place so that other states and other organizations can’t attack that,” he reportedly added. “They can’t do things like they’re doing with mailing in mail-order drugs.”

The Independent has contacted the Department of Justice for comment.

The Justice Department previously told The Independent that the comments “need to be understood in their full context, which was with respect to mail order abortion drugs, not a broader expansion of federal control over states.”

Much to the chagrin of anti-abortion campaigners, abortions have actually increased since the constitutional right to abortion care was struck down at the Supreme Court, thanks to a mix of expanded telehealth access, Biden-era policies and blue state “shield laws” protecting physicians who provide abortion care.

While much of the attention in Blanche’s confirmation was directed at a now-abandoned $1.8 billion“slush fund” for the president’s political allies and a provision that shields the president from IRS investigations, Blanche’s appointment battle suggests the Trump administration could pursue more restrictions on abortion access.

open image in gallery Republicans are pushing the DOJ to settle cases challenging access to mifepristone, a commonly used abortion pill ( AFP/Getty )

Under questioning, he committed to reviewing the the Justice Department’s interpretation of the 1873 Comstock Act, which makes it illegal to send a variety of objects including “abortion-causing articles” via mail.

A 2022 Justice Department opinion held that the law doesn’t inherently bar sending abortion medication, given that “there are manifold ways in which recipients in every state may lawfully use such drugs, including to produce an abortion.”

On the campaign trail, Donald Trump described regulation around mail-order abortion drugs as a state issue, rather than a federal one, adding that he wouldn’t use the 19th century law to crack down on abortion access.

“The federal government should have nothing to do with this issue,” he said in 2024.

Republicans in the Senate have also pushed the federal government to settle lawsuits around mifepristone, a widely used abortion drug.

During his confirmation hearing, Blanche pointed to the FDA’s ongoing review of mifepristone. In 2023, the Biden administration ended in-person dispensing requirements around the drug, prompting challenges in Republican states.

“We have to have studies that we can defend in court,” he told senators in July.

In May, the Supreme Court continued to block nationwide restrictions on mifepristone after a conservative appeals court cut off mail-order and telehealth access the drug, threatening access to millions of patients.

The president has vowed to be “the most pro-life and pro-family president in American history.”

In 2022, the Supreme Court, thanks to the conservative supermajority Trump helped appoint, overturned the landmark 1973 decision in Roe v Wade, which had established a constitutional right to an abortion.

News.title: Extremist 764 group allegedly linked to Southern California hospital bomb threat
News.content:

Federal authorities were investigating a bomb threat at Huntington Hospital in Pasadena on Saturday after an evacuation was prompted by a caller who allegedly identified himself as a member of the extremist online group 764.

The call was received at around 5:50 a.m. Friday, according to Pasadena spokeswoman Lisa Derderian.

The Pasadena Police Department said the caller claimed multiple explosive devices had been placed throughout the hospital and alleged that two additional suspects were heading to the facility in a stolen vehicle. The caller also claimed the suspects intended to shoot people with automatic rifles.

Officers responded to the hospital and worked with security to secure all entrances while establishing a strong law enforcement presence around the facility.

Police set up a command post in the parking lot of a nearby business and called in multiple K9 units. The Pasadena Fire Department also responded and remained on standby to assist if needed.

The caller also claimed the suspects intended to shoot people with automatic rifles ( Andrew Leyden/Getty Images )

Pasadena and Glendale police K9 units searched and cleared all publicly accessible areas of the hospital but found no explosive devices, police said.

As a precaution, incoming emergency traffic was diverted to nearby hospitals after the bomb threat was reported. Once the hospital was deemed safe, normal operations resumed.

The hospital was declared safe shortly after 9 a.m. Friday.

Although no one was injured in Friday’s threat, Derderian said such incidents are “very disruptive” and divert valuable resources from law enforcement and fire response teams.

The FBI has described 764 as "a violent online group made-up of individuals who seek to coerce and manipulate children into engaging in unspeakable acts against themselves, animals, and other children, even suicide."

Members of the group exist throughout the United States and around the world and operate on social media, gaming apps and online platforms, authorities said. Officials added that the group is also known to engage in "swatting" -- placing false emergency calls to trigger armed police raids.

Southern California has previously been targeted by swatting calls involving hospitals. In April, a bomb threat at Southern California Hospital in the Culver City area prompted a response from explosives-detection K-9 units and was ultimately determined to be a swatting incident. No explosive device was found.

British Columbia has declared a state of emergency as a rapidly spreading wildfire devastates communities, forcing over 20,000 residents to evacuate their homes along Okanagan Lake in western Canada.

Premier David Eby announced the emergency Saturday, with over 100 wildfires currently raging across the province. Nearly half of these blazes are out of control, fueled by hot, windy conditions and a prolonged drought.

The entire community of Summerland, home to approximately 12,000 people, received overnight evacuation orders, alongside 8,000 individuals in and around nearby Peachland. Officials have yet to determine how many homes were destroyed.

Eby confirmed some residents became trapped and required rescue, while search-and-rescue teams continue to comb areas behind fire lines for any others who may have been caught.

Nearly half of these blazes are out of control, fueled by hot, windy conditions and a prolonged drought ( Gary Nylander/The Canadian Press via AP )

“I know many families are facing an unimaginable day today,” Eby said. “People have lost their homes. And many people have been displaced. Others are waiting for news about loved ones.”

Cliff Chapman, director of wildfire operations for the BC Wildfire Service, said firefighting helicopters were diverted to rescue people who could no longer escape by road. He said the outcome would have been significantly worse without cooperation among agencies responding to the fire.

The Bald Range wildfire was first reported on Friday evening but grew to about 50 square kilometers (19 square miles) within hours, overwhelming the smaller community of Faulder and covering the roughly 15 kilometers (9 miles) to Summerland at extraordinary speed.

Chapman described fire conditions across British Columbia as “explosive” and warned that other communities could face fires similar to the one that forced the evacuation of Summerland.

British Columbia Emergency Management Minister Kelly Greene said the state of emergency gives the province additional powers, including the ability to restrict travel and secure accommodations for evacuees that might otherwise be unavailable.

Erick Thompson, an emergency official with the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen, called it one of the “quickest-moving, fastest-growing” wildfires the region had experienced.

Thompson eventually had to abandon the emergency operations center and evacuate his own family.

“I had to leave the EOC to come and get my family to leave this area. We’re heading south,” he said in a video posted early Saturday from his vehicle as traffic backed up around him.

Videos posted on social media appeared to show multiple homes burning as residents fled along roads with flames on both sides.

Homeowner Kerry Gold and her husband, Mike Elsinga, fled around 12:30 a.m. after watching flames spread beyond nearby mountains.

“It’s scary. It’s moving fast,” Gold said.

The couple, who recently moved from the city of Vancouver, had packed bags, prepared a carrier for their cat and planned to help a disabled friend evacuate.

“You want to stay here and protect your home, but you also don’t want to get caught in it,” Elsinga said.

Canada has endured increasingly destructive wildfire seasons in recent years, forcing mass evacuations and repeatedly sending smoke across large parts of Canada and the United States.

News.title: Huge wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday as officials declared a state of emergency.

The fire in Bald Range doubled in size overnight on Friday, spreading rapidly to about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across British Columbia, including Summerland, Peachland and other districts west of Okanagan Lake.

The region produces most of British Columbia’s wine and is Canada’s second-largest wine-producing area.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had likened the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

News.title: Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan
News.content:
Chelsea 3 AC Milan 0

Chelsea cruised to a 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head intothe break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto. Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.
